findings.claim: Optional and non-blocking. The new 'insertion order' assertion cannot tell sequence order apart from scope or index order. This is because the fixture inserts the Project, Goal and Task rows in the same order that usage_by_scope(project_id, goal_id, task_id) sorts them, with NULLs first.
findings.evidence: In the fixture, the rows are inserted P(NULL,NULL), G(g,NULL), T(g,t). SQLite sorts NULL before any value, so an `ORDER BY goal_id,task_id` mutant returns exactly json!(valid) and survives. Removing ORDER BY so that the usage_by_scope index order is used would very likely survive too. Every other usage test has a single row. The production ORDER BY is unchanged from baseline and no ordering mutant is claimed, so this concerns control strength, not correctness. The test comment at 907-908 and the doc text 'exact ordered selected rows' imply more than the assertion discriminates.
findings.fix: Insert the Task-scoped row first, or interleave the rows, so that sequence order differs from scope/index order. Optionally record an ORDER BY mutant. Not required for this component.
